request-and-reply.title: Create sockets and exchange frames
request-and-reply.note: The client and server are separate Python processes. Read queue admission separately from the application reply.
request-and-reply.question: Does send_string returning prove that the handler completed its work?
request-and-reply.answer: No. It establishes local send behavior. An application reply is separate evidence, and its business meaning depends on the protocol.

preserve-message-frames.title: Send and receive one multipart message
preserve-message-frames.note: Read the sequence-of-bytes contract, including an empty frame.
preserve-message-frames.question: Does an empty final frame mean that the receiver got no message?
preserve-message-frames.answer: No. It is a zero-byte frame inside a received multipart message. Frame boundaries and message boundaries are separate from payload length.

respect-the-req-state-machine.title: REQ send/receive ordering
respect-the-req-state-machine.note: Read the permitted order of operations for the REQ pattern.
respect-the-req-state-machine.question: Does receiving the first reply permit a second send?
respect-the-req-state-machine.answer: Yes. A normal REQ alternates send then receive. Trying the second send before that receive violates its state machine.

send-work-down-a-pipeline.title: Push jobs and pull them
send-work-down-a-pipeline.note: Read serialization separately from the PUSH/PULL distribution pattern.
send-work-down-a-pipeline.question: Does one PUSH job go to every connected PULL worker?
send-work-down-a-pipeline.answer: No. A pipeline distributes work among available peers; it is not a publication broadcast.

filter-a-publication.title: Subscribe to a byte prefix
filter-a-publication.note: The subscription matches the beginning of the first frame, not a parsed topic hierarchy.
filter-a-publication.question: Does a prefix of order match only the exact topic order?
filter-a-publication.answer: No. It also matches topics beginning with those bytes, such as orders. An empty prefix subscribes to every message.

meet-the-late-subscriber.title: Wait for subscription evidence
meet-the-late-subscriber.note: XPUB can expose subscription control messages. Receiving that evidence is different from replaying earlier publications.
meet-the-late-subscriber.question: Does a new SUB socket automatically recover messages published before its subscription became active?
meet-the-late-subscriber.answer: No. PUB/SUB provides no durable replay history. This helper contrasts an early publication with publication after observed subscription readiness.

detect-a-sequence-gap.title: Read a publication and inspect its sequence
detect-a-sequence-gap.note: The helper authors the sequence numbers and gap detector; neither is inferred by recv_multipart.
detect-a-sequence-gap.question: Can noticing a missing sequence number reconstruct the missing payload?
detect-a-sequence-gap.answer: No. It identifies an observed gap under the chosen sequence contract. Recovery requires a replay source or another application protocol.

receive-without-blocking.title: Nonblocking receive and Again
receive-without-blocking.note: Read the exception raised when no message can be received immediately.
receive-without-blocking.question: Is b"" the same observation as an Again exception?
receive-without-blocking.answer: No. b"" is a successfully received zero-byte message. Again means no message was received by that nonblocking call.

bound-a-socket-queue.title: Bound outgoing and incoming queues
bound-a-socket-queue.note: Read high-water marks and the pattern-specific response to a full queue.
bound-a-socket-queue.question: Does SNDHWM=2 guarantee the process holds at most two messages in total?
bound-a-socket-queue.answer: No. Queue boundaries, peers and transports matter; the option is not a whole-process memory bound. The helper measures actual admission in its bounded fixture.

route-an-envelope.title: Route by identity and preserve the envelope
route-an-envelope.note: Read how the ROUTER identity frame is used to choose the next peer.
route-an-envelope.question: Is the routing frame automatically the application request ID?
route-an-envelope.answer: No. It identifies a route. The application must separately define request identity and the meaning of the remaining frames.

reject-an-unknown-route.title: Make missing routes observable
reject-an-unknown-route.note: Read the behavior when a ROUTER has no route for the supplied identity.
reject-an-unknown-route.question: Does enabling ROUTER_MANDATORY prove an existing worker handled a message?
reject-an-unknown-route.answer: No. It can make a missing route fail visibly, but route admission is still different from application completion.

match-out-of-order-replies.title: Separate routing from correlation
match-out-of-order-replies.note: The helper supplies application request IDs and matches replies by those IDs.
match-out-of-order-replies.question: If two replies arrive in reverse order, should the caller assign them by position in the receive list?
match-out-of-order-replies.answer: No. Match each reply to its application ID. Socket routing alone does not infer the business request being answered.

forward-through-a-proxy.title: Forward between frontend and backend
forward-through-a-proxy.note: The separate peer process calls the real zmq.proxy function. The client and worker still own the application protocol.
forward-through-a-proxy.question: Does proxy executing establish that a worker committed a job?
forward-through-a-proxy.answer: No. It forwards messages between sockets. A worker reply or durable receipt must define completion.

retry-with-stable-identity.title: Poll with a deadline and retry deliberately
retry-with-stable-identity.note: The deadline controls waiting. The helper keeps the same application ID and implements duplicate suppression.
retry-with-stable-identity.question: Does a poll timeout prove that the first attempt had no effect?
retry-with-stable-identity.answer: No. A reply may be delayed or lost after an effect. A retry needs an identity and an explicit effect/receipt contract.

dispatch-with-worker-credit.title: Application readiness above routed sockets
dispatch-with-worker-credit.note: The READY/DONE messages and returned credits are authored application messages, not a ZeroMQ worker scheduler.
dispatch-with-worker-credit.question: Does a known routing identity mean the worker has spare capacity?
dispatch-with-worker-credit.answer: No. The broker’s credit policy supplies that information. The fixture can withhold a returned credit to show the distinction.

replay-a-cached-value.title: Subscription controls and cached replay
replay-a-cached-value.note: The helper stores a latest value and decides what to replay after subscription evidence.
replay-a-cached-value.question: Is this helper’s latest-value cache a durable PUB/SUB log?
replay-a-cached-value.answer: No. It is a volatile application cache with a chosen replay rule; neither publication history nor process-crash recovery is guaranteed.

observe-a-connection.title: Observe transport events
observe-a-connection.note: Read how monitor events report connection changes and compare them with an application reply.
observe-a-connection.question: Does CONNECTED mean that the server has processed the request?
observe-a-connection.answer: No. It is transport evidence. The helper also performs an application exchange to make that separate observation visible.

choose-connect-and-close-policy.title: Admission at connect time and closing queues
choose-connect-and-close-policy.note: Read which peers can accept a send and how pending messages are treated on close.
choose-connect-and-close-policy.question: With LINGER=0, must pending messages have reached a receiver before close returns?
choose-connect-and-close-policy.answer: No. Pending messages can be discarded. IMMEDIATE and linger solve different parts of the admission/shutdown contract.

encrypt-a-connection.title: Generate keys and configure CURVE
encrypt-a-connection.note: Read server-key configuration separately from the application’s authorization decision.
encrypt-a-connection.question: Does a successful CURVE exchange prove the caller is allowed to submit every job?
encrypt-a-connection.answer: No. Transport protection and authentication evidence do not define the service’s authorization policy.

diagnose-the-missing-receipt.title: Reconcile reply matching and retries
diagnose-the-missing-receipt.note: The capstone composes the course correlation and retry helpers. Read the socket contracts while accounting for attempts and effects separately.
diagnose-the-missing-receipt.question: Can fewer visible receipts prove that fewer attempts reached a handler?
diagnose-the-missing-receipt.answer: No. Missing replies leave uncertainty. Use stable identities, recorded effects and a defined receipt contract rather than inferring completion from a count.
